root_cause.text: btrfs_create_new_inode() updated filesystem state before validating that a colliding directory name could still fit in the existing hashed dir item, so a dir-item size overflow from name-hash collisions was treated as a fatal post-update error and aborted the transaction.
root_cause.evidence: The commit message states that colliding names must be packed into the same dir item with a leaf-size limit and that reaching this limit “trigger[s] a transaction abort”; the patch adds an early btrfs_check_dir_item_collision() call in btrfs_create_new_inode() “before we do any tree updates” specifically “to avoid a transaction abort.”

intent_record.intent_summary: Pre-check directory item collisions during regular inode creation to fail safely before link insertion and avoid transaction aborts.
intent_record.what: A new conditional block was added at the start of btrfs_create_new_inode() that, when args->orphan is false and args->subvol is false, calls btrfs_check_dir_item_collision() with the parent directory root, inode number, and name, and immediately returns on any negative error before allocating the path.
intent_record.how: This makes regular inode creation fail early if adding the new name to the parent directory would hit a directory item collision/overflow condition, preventing the later btrfs_add_link() path from triggering a transaction abort; orphan and subvolume cases are excluded because the check is not needed there or is already handled elsewhere.

grouping_result.intent: Pre-check directory item collisions during regular inode creation to fail safely before link insertion and avoid transaction aborts.

relevance_review.reason: The change directly matches the root cause: it adds a pre-check for colliding directory items before inode/link insertion, preventing post-update dir-item size overflow errors from aborting the transaction.
